- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment drops below 0.3 in 3–5 days, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect weakening bearish sentiment.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1st–5th day); add 0.5–1.5% bias to first 5 forecast points.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model shows mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward 3–5-day moving average of history.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day weighted average.
